correctness.rationale: For periodic piecewise C1 V with one well per period, the reset-to-current-well process is a renewal-reward walk: v(r)=rL E[K_tau]. The harmonic coordinate h(x)=(L/Z+) integral_0^x e^V is periodic modulo linear lift and satisfies generator harmonicity; optional stopping yields E[K_tau]=-E[h(Y_tau)]/L. As r->0, the mod-L diffusion approaches invariant e^-V/Z-, yielding m(0+)=(J_L-J_R)/(Z+Z-). For explicit A=11/10>B=1, the source integral bounds give J_L<121/350<15471/40000<J_R, so v<0 at small rate. For r large, bounded-drift Gaussian exponential stopping tails imply the positive nearest right crossing at distance B dominates negative left crossings at A>B, so v>0. Continuity forces >=1 reversal; convolution gives nondegenerate unique minimum and maximum preserving strict signs. Independent piecewise-affine quadrature checked J_L~0.343438923 and J_R~0.440504587; only finite sanity tests, not an existence-of-unique-zero claim.

Prior local-reset ratchet models and flashing-phase current reversal differ, and the same-model 2023 preprint studied current with one sign for its chosen example rather than this constructive reversal.
